Unit 6 • SL

Data & Information

Introduction

How do you structure data so it stays accurate as systems grow?

This unit focuses on relational data design. You will study how databases use tables, keys, and constraints to maintain integrity and reduce redundancy.

You will explain the strengths and limits of relational databases, describe conceptual/logical/physical schema levels, explain how 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF differ, and outline the role of SQL language types: DDL and DML.

Relational structure

Relational systems store data in linked tables.

  • Primary keys identify records uniquely.
  • Foreign keys connect related tables.
  • Referential integrity prevents invalid relationships.

Schema levels

Schemas describe database architecture at different levels:

  • Conceptual: entities and relationships.
  • Logical: fields, keys, and constraints.
  • Physical: DBMS implementation and access strategy.

Normalization

Normalization improves consistency and reduces anomalies:

  • 1NF: atomic values, no repeating groups.
  • 2NF: no partial dependency on a composite key.
  • 3NF: no transitive dependency between non-key fields.

SQL language types

SQL is grouped by purpose:

  • DDL: define/modify structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP).
  • DML: query and update rows (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Relational DatabaseA database that stores linked data in tables using keys and constraints.
Primary KeyA field or set of fields that uniquely identifies each record in a table.
Foreign KeyA field that references a primary key in another table.
SchemaThe defined structure of a database and its relationships.
Conceptual SchemaA high-level representation of entities and relationships.
Logical SchemaDetailed table design including attributes, keys, and constraints.
Physical SchemaHow the database is implemented in a specific DBMS.
NormalizationOrganizing tables to reduce redundancy and improve integrity.
1NF / 2NF / 3NFSuccessive normal forms based on atomicity and dependency rules.
DDL / DMLSQL categories for structure management and data manipulation.

Common Misconceptions

Normalization is just sorting data

Normalization is a dependency-based redesign process, not row sorting.

Cardinality and modality are the same

Cardinality describes maximum relationship count; modality describes minimum participation.

Relational tables map directly to OOP classes

Relational models and object models overlap, but they are not equivalent structures.

Real-World Uses

  • School student information and timetable systems
  • Online ordering and stock tracking
  • Healthcare appointment databases
  • Banking account and transaction records
  • Library and borrowing systems

Think Deeper

"Can perfect structure ever capture messy real-world information?" Database design improves consistency, but every schema is a model with assumptions and trade-offs.
